co2_src.name: Nab & Maslin 2020, Geo: Geography and Environment (summarised by UCL / The Conversation)
co2_src.note: Peer-reviewed LCA synthesis, conventional Arabica from Brazil/Vietnam exported to UK; one espresso made with ~18 g green coffee, no milk, cup not included. Latte 0.55 kg. ADEME Agribalyse 3.2 gives 0.635 kg/L brewed coffee incl. packaging (about 0.16 kg per 250 ml), so the plausible range is ~0.1-0.3 kg.

water_src.name: Water Footprint Network product gallery (Mekonnen & Hoekstra 2010/2011)
water_src.note: TOTAL water footprint (96% green, 1% blue = ~1.3 L, 3% grey) for a 125 ml cup made with 7 g roasted coffee. Global average, 1996-2005 data.

volume_src.name: USDA FAS, Coffee: World Markets and Trade (July 2026)
volume_src.note: World consumption 2025/26 = 173.459 million 60-kg bags (green bean equivalent) = 10.41 Mt; divided by 18 g green coffee per cup (same dose as the CO2 figure). DERIVED. At WFN's 7 g roasted (~8.5 g green) per cup the count would be roughly double (~1.2 trillion).

swap.label: Sustainably grown beans (and skip dairy milk)

src.name: Nab & Maslin 2020 via UCL
src.note: Espresso falls from 0.28 to 0.06 kg CO2e with sustainably produced coffee. A reusable cup alone saves much less, because the beans dominate the footprint (estimate, no source).

products.name: Single-use plastic water bottle (0.5 L PET)

co2_src.name: ADEME Impact CO2 (Agribalyse 3.2, updated 2025-01-15), 'Eau en bouteille'
co2_src.note: Cradle-to-grave 321 g CO2e per litre (packaging 58%, transport 36%), halved for 0.5 L. French market; small bottles carry more PET per litre, so likely an underestimate. Cross-check: NIH NEMS review sums resin 0.038-0.063 + bottle forming 0.034-0.046 kg per 500 ml bottle (~0.09 kg, excl. transport and chilling): https://nems.nih.gov/Documents/PETWaterBottlesEnvironmentalImpact.pdf

water_src.name: Pacific Institute, Bottled Water and Energy Fact Sheet (Gleick)
water_src.note: BLUE (withdrawn) water: ~3 L of water used to produce 1 L of bottled water (2006 US data), scaled to 0.5 L; includes the water in the bottle. Old, US-only.

volume_src.name: UNEP, 'Our planet is drowning in plastic pollution'
volume_src.note: 'One million plastic drinking bottles are purchased every minute' = 525.6 billion/yr. Covers ALL plastic drink bottles, not only 0.5 L water. Traces to Euromonitor data (480 billion bottles in 2016, Guardian 2017).

swap.label: Refill a reusable bottle with tap water

src.name: ADEME Impact CO2, 'Eau du robinet'
src.note: Tap water 0.132 g CO2e/L vs bottled 321 g/L (>99.9% lower). Excludes making the reusable bottle itself, which is small once amortised over many refills.

co2_src.name: Poore & Nemecek 2018, Science (via Our World in Data)
co2_src.note: Global mean 99.48 kg CO2e per kg beef (beef herd), farm-to-retail, x 0.113 kg. Patty only, no bun. Beef from dairy herds is 33.3 kg/kg (= 3.76 kg per patty); US beef is far below the global mean, so this is the high, global-average case.

water_src.name: Water Footprint Network product gallery (Mekonnen & Hoekstra 2012)
water_src.note: TOTAL water footprint 15,415 L/kg beef (94% green, 4% blue = ~70 L per patty, 3% grey), x 0.113 kg. Mostly rain-fed feed crops and pasture.

volume_src.name: USDA FAS, Livestock and Poultry: World Markets and Trade (Oct 2026)
volume_src.note: World beef & veal consumption 2025 = 60.353 Mt carcass-weight equivalent, divided by 0.113 kg = quarter-pound-EQUIVALENTS of beef, not burgers actually sold. DERIVED. Carcass weight overstates edible meat (~30%), so treat as an upper bound.

src.name: Heller & Keoleian 2018, Univ. of Michigan CSS report CSS18-10 (commissioned by Beyond Meat)
src.note: Beyond Burger vs 1/4 lb US beef, cradle-to-distribution: 90% less GHG, 46% less energy, >99% less water-scarcity impact, 93% less land.

co2_src.name: ADEME Impact CO2 / Base Empreinte, 'T-shirt en coton'
co2_src.note: Cradle-to-grave: manufacturing 5.2 kg (81%), use (washing over 5 years) + end of life 1.23 kg. Published LCAs range ~1.7-8.8 kg. No authoritative average-garment figure exists; a crude top-down 1.2 Gt CO2e textiles production (Ellen MacArthur Foundation 2017) / ~100 billion garments (McKinsey 2016) gives ~12 kg per item (ESTIMATE, includes non-clothing textiles).

water_src.name: Water Footprint Network product gallery (Mekonnen & Hoekstra 2010/2011)
water_src.note: TOTAL water footprint for a 250 g cotton shirt (54% green, 33% blue = ~823 L, 13% grey). A lighter T-shirt (~150-200 g) would be proportionally lower.

volume_src.name: McKinsey & Co., 'Style that's sustainable' (2016)
volume_src.note: Garments produced per year 'exceeded 100 billion for the first time in 2014' (all clothing, not only T-shirts). Old; current volume is likely higher but no better primary figure was found.

src.name: Klooster et al. 2024, Journal of Circular Economy 2(1), doi:10.55845/ZZUG7076
src.note: Peer-reviewed LCA of second-hand T-shirts, dresses, trousers, sweaters: 'up to 42%' lower climate impact per use within the same behaviour scenario. Benefit disappears if the item is rarely worn.

co2_src.name: Cheah, Olivetti, Kirchain et al. 2013, Journal of Cleaner Production (MIT News summary)
co2_src.note: Cradle-to-grave LCA of a synthetic ASICS running shoe made in China: 14 +/- 2.7 kg CO2e (MIT News: '30 pounds'); ~2/3 from manufacturing. ADEME Impact CO2 gives 20.1 kg for 'paire de chaussures de sport' (https://impactco2.fr/outils/habillement/chaussuresdesport).

water_src.name: none found
water_src.note: No credible per-pair water footprint for synthetic sneakers. WFN bovine leather is 17,093 L/kg and FoE/Trucost (2015) put a pair of LEATHER boots at ~14,500 L, but these do not apply to mostly synthetic sneakers.

volume_src.name: APICCAPS World Footwear Yearbook 2026 (via worldfootwear.com, 2026-08-04)
volume_src.note: 24.6 billion pairs of ALL footwear produced in 2025. No credible sneaker-only count found, so this is an upper bound for sneakers.

src.name: estimate
src.note: Estimate: use phase is negligible (MIT), so doubling wear life roughly halves emissions per year of use.

co2_src.name: Apple, iPhone 17 Product Environmental Report (Sept 2025)
co2_src.note: Life cycle (ISO 14040/44/67), 256 GB US config incl. packaging: production 77% (materials 23% + manufacturing electricity 53% + renewable-energy emissions 1%), charging over 3 yrs 18%, transport 4%, end of life <1%. 512 GB = 61 kg. Still Apple's current base iPhone (iPhone 18 PER covers Pro models only). Market average per ADEME/ARCEP 2025: 80.2 kg, 99% manufacturing (https://impactco2.fr/outils/numerique/smartphone).

water_src.name: Friends of the Earth / Trucost, 'Mind your step' (May 2015)
water_src.note: TOTAL supply-chain water footprint, 'nearly 13 tonnes' per smartphone, about two-fifths of it grey water (pollution) from component manufacturing. Generic phone, old, model-based.

cobalt_src.name: Washington Post, 'The cobalt pipeline' (Frankel, 2016)
cobalt_src.note: 'A smartphone battery might contain five to 10 grams of refined cobalt'; 7.5 g is the midpoint. Investigative journalism, not a lab measurement. iPhone 17 battery uses 100% recycled cobalt (Apple PER).

volume_src.name: IDC Worldwide Quarterly Mobile Phone Tracker, press release 2026-01-13
volume_src.note: 1.26 billion smartphones shipped worldwide in 2025 (preliminary), +1.9% YoY.

src.name: ADEME 2022, Assessment of the environmental impact of a set of refurbished products
src.note: Refurbished phone used 2 yrs instead of a new one used 3 yrs avoids 24.6 kg CO2e per year = -87% climate impact per year of use (reference scenario).

co2_src.name: Apple, MacBook Air (M5) Product Environmental Report (Mar 2026)
co2_src.note: Life cycle, 13-inch M5 / 16 GB / 512 GB = 119 kg CO2e (15-inch = 145 kg). Stage split is published only for the 15-inch: production 63% (materials 24% + electricity 38% + renewable 1%), use over 4 yrs 27%, transport 10%, EoL <1%; applied to the 13-inch as an approximation. Market average per ADEME/ARCEP 2025: 193 kg (14.6-inch), 95% manufacturing (https://impactco2.fr/outils/numerique/ordinateurportable).

water_src.name: none found
water_src.note: No credible, citable per-laptop water footprint found (Apple PERs give no per-unit water figure).

cobalt_src.name: Washington Post, 'The cobalt pipeline' (Frankel, 2016)
cobalt_src.note: Graphic: a laptop contains about '1 ounce' (28 g) of cobalt. 2016 figure; laptop cathode chemistries vary and many now use less cobalt. MacBook Air M5 battery uses 100% recycled cobalt (Apple PER).

volume_src.name: Omdia press release 2026-01-12
volume_src.note: Notebook (incl. mobile workstation) shipments 219.7 million in 2025, +7.5%. All sizes. Total PCs 278.7 M (Gartner: >270 M).

swap.label: Buy refurbished or keep it longer

src.name: ADEME 2022, Assessment of the environmental impact of a set of refurbished products
src.note: Refurbished laptop used 3 yrs instead of a new one used 5 yrs avoids 27.3 kg CO2e per year = -77% climate impact per year of use.

car_t_per_year.name: US EPA, Greenhouse Gas Emissions from a Typical Passenger Vehicle (page updated 2026-06-03)
car_t_per_year.note: Tailpipe CO2 only: ~4.6 t/yr, assumes 22.2 mpg and ~11,500 miles/yr (EPA-420-F-23-014).

car_kg_per_km.name: US EPA, same page
car_kg_per_km.note: ~400 g CO2 per mile tailpipe = 0.2485 kg per km (DERIVED unit conversion).

shower_l.name: US EPA WaterSense, Specification for Showerheads Supporting Statement
shower_l.note: Assumes 17.2 gallons per shower (8.2 min average) = 65.1 L. Newer EPA consumer material says '8 minutes x 2.1 gpm = more than 16 gallons' (~61 L).

budget_t.name: Hot or Cool Institute, 1.5-Degree Lifestyles: Towards a Fair Consumption Space for All
budget_t.note: Per-capita lifestyle carbon footprint target compatible with 1.5C: 2.5 t CO2e by 2030, 1.4 t by 2040, 0.7 t by 2050 (builds on IGES et al. 2019).

src.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, Cobalt
src.note: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 (first posted 2026-02-06), world total (rounded); production = 2025 estimated mine production. Congo (Kinshasa) ~73% of mine output.

src.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, Nickel
src.note: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 (first posted 2026-02-06), world total (rounded); production = 2025 estimated mine production. Reserves are reported as '>140,000,000' t (a lower bound). Indonesia 2.6 Mt of 2025 output.

src.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, Copper
src.note: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 (first posted 2026-02-06), world total (rounded); production = 2025 estimated mine production. Table is in thousand metric tons (23,000 kt mine; 980,000 kt reserves). Refinery output 29 Mt.

src.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, Lithium
src.note: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 (first posted 2026-02-06), world total (rounded); production = 2025 estimated mine production. Lithium content; world production total excludes US output (withheld).

meta.notes: Figures mix cradle-to-grave and cradle-to-retail boundaries; see each src.note. DERIVED marks values computed from cited inputs.
